name: The Missing Moment
brief: A daughter asks AI to restore a face in an old photograph. Two plausible answers make her question what belongs in a family album. Keep the human action quiet, the photograph tangible and the ending open. This editable scene study uses original references and native takes. It is not a frame-identical copy of the finished film.

shots.name: A page for Mum
shots.note: Mum was coming round. I wanted to finish something for her. A page for the family album.

shots.name: The missing face
shots.note: That's her, when she was five. The garden's still there. Her face is gone.

shots.name: A simple request
shots.note: Can you fill in the bit that's missing?

shots.name: A possible smile
shots.note: And there she was. A little smile. I thought, yes. That looks like Mum.

shots.name: Two possibilities
shots.note: This time, she wasn't smiling. I liked the first one better. But that didn't make it right.

shots.name: Explaining a guess
shots.note: I asked why it had chosen a smile. The answer sounded reasonable. But it was still explaining a guess.

shots.name: What becomes a memory
shots.note: If I put this in the album, someone might think it was real. In a few years, I might think so too.

shots.name: The honest archive
shots.note: I kept the old photograph. Beside the new one, I wrote: imagined. I didn't want to lose what was real.

shots.name: The garden
shots.note: Mum was still sitting across from me.

subtitles.text: Mum was coming round. I wanted to finish something for her.
A page for the family album.
That's her, when she was five. The garden's still there.
Her face is gone.
Can you fill in the bit that's missing?
And there she was. A little smile.
I thought, yes. That looks like Mum.
Could you try another one?
This time, she wasn't smiling.
I liked the first one better.
But that didn't make it right.
I asked why it had chosen a smile.
The answer sounded reasonable.
But it was still explaining a guess.
If I put this in the album, someone might think it was real.
In a few years, I might think so too.
Then Mum arrived.
Do you remember this?
Oh, I don't remember that day.
That's all right.
I kept the old photograph.
Beside the new one, I wrote: imagined.
I didn't want to lose what was real.
Mum was still sitting across from me.
What was the garden like?
There were roses by the back door.
Your grandad was very proud of them.
